newsitem.title: GERMANY: HIGHER UKRAINE SUNSEED CROP SEEN - OIL WORLD.
newsitem.headline: HIGHER UKRAINE SUNSEED CROP SEEN - OIL WORLD.

text.p: Ukraine may produce 2.5-2.7 million tonnes of sunflowerseed in 1997, up from an estimated 2.3 million tonnes in 1996, the independent Oil World newsletter said on Tuesday.
It also said Russia's crop should be somewhere between 2.8 and 3.0 million tonnes -- close to last year's level, according to Oil World.
Other forecasts for 1997 in recent weeks have indicated 2.5-3.2 million for Russia and 2.5-2.9 million for Ukraine.
The official Ukrainian 1996 crop figure is 2.04 million tonnes and Russia's 2.75 million.
Oil World said the Ukrainian sunseed area was virtually unchanged from last year's 2.03 million hectares.
Rain patterns and yield prospects were favourable in both countries, where sunseed is an important cash crop.
Domestic supply from the old crop was tight in Ukraine so exports had been sharply reduced, Oil World said.
In June, they totalled just 15,000 tonnes after 51,000 tonnes in June 1996.
But the cumulative September/June 1996/97 total was still at a record 965,000 tonnes versus 357,000 in the previous season.
Livestock reductions were curtailing domestic meal demand.
